title: NestJS Quiz
description: Review the 12 starter lessons. The questions name the example to revisit. Take your time, use the lessons, and read the reason after each answer.

questions.question: A controller holds request handlers. @Get maps GET /hello to its method. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The module lists the controller. The Get decorator maps hello to /hello and Nest sends its returned string. A controller must be listed in a module to be used.

questions.question: Nest sends returned objects as JSON. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The controller returns an object. Nest serialises title and pages into JSON. Let Nest write the returned object instead of writing a second response.

questions.question: @Param reads a named part of the route. Open GET /hello/Ravi. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The Param decorator takes the name segment from the URL. The handler receives Ravi. A TypeScript type does not validate a value sent over HTTP.

questions.question: @Query reads the query string. Visit GET /search?q=cat. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The Query decorator supplies q from the URL. Its value becomes the term field. Validate query input before using it for important work.

questions.question: ParseIntPipe reads an integer or rejects bad input. GET /double/4 uses the checked number. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: ParseIntPipe converts 4 before the method runs. Multiplying the resulting number gives 8. The pipe does the runtime check; the number annotation alone does not.

questions.question: @Body supplies parsed JSON. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Body supplies the parsed object. The string check passes and its title is returned. Check body fields instead of trusting the TypeScript shape.

questions.question: A provider is a shared helper supplied by Nest. The controller asks for Books in its constructor. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The module creates Books as a provider. Constructor injection gives the same helper to the controller. List Books in module providers so Nest can create it.

questions.question: DefaultValuePipe supplies a value before ParseIntPipe checks it. Open GET /page with no query. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The default pipe supplies 1 for the missing query input. The integer pipe then checks it. Pipe order matters: the default should happen before parsing.

questions.question: @HttpCode changes a handler status. POST /check returns 200 instead of the usual Nest POST status. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: HttpCode overrides the usual POST status. The returned object still controls the JSON body. A status describes the reply; it does not change the returned data.

questions.question: @Header adds metadata to a response. Open GET /note and inspect its Cache-Control header. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The Header decorator adds no-store before Nest sends the text. Headers must be set before a response is sent.

questions.question: @Redirect sends a location to the client. A browser following GET /start ends at /hello. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Redirect sends a 302 with /hello as its location. The browser then requests the greeting route. A redirect makes the client send a new request.

questions.question: A built-in exception creates an HTTP error response. GET /missing reports a missing book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: NotFoundException stops the normal result path and creates an HTTP 404 error with the supplied message. Use a suitable HTTP error instead of returning a success status for a failure.
